proposed_relationship: The mechanical cleavage of graphite can produce a two-dimensional crystal of carbon with useful electronic properties, potentially stable at finite temperature due to its small size.
mechanism: The mechanism involves using mechanical cleavage to thin layered graphite samples, resulting in the creation of a single atomic sheet of carbon, which is a two-dimensional crystal. This process may release the constraint imposed by the Landau-Peierls theory, as the small size of the resulting crystal could limit the long-wavelength fluctuations that make strictly two-dimensional crystals thermodynamically unstable. The resulting two-dimensional crystal of carbon would have useful electronic properties, similar to those of carbon nanotubes.
constraint_released: The constraint of thermodynamic instability of two-dimensional crystals at finite temperature due to long-wavelength fluctuations is released by reducing the size of the crystal.
predicted_quantitative_outcome: 10^-9 meters, the predicted size of the resulting two-dimensional crystal of carbon
